company.name: Lumen Legal
company.summary: Lumen Legal is a 45 person law firm in Antwerp, Belgium. You and your team advise employers and companies on employment and commercial law, draft and review contracts, track deadlines, and handle time registration and billing. Your clients are businesses that need practical legal support in Belgium.
company.customers: Businesses, employers, and companies in Belgium, from small firms to larger enterprises needing employment and commercial law support.

strategy.executive_summary: Lumen Legal is a 45 person firm where most of the work is done by hand: deadlines written into calendars one by one, contracts read end to end, time entries checked line by line, and clients answered from a shared inbox. You already have Microsoft 365, a practice management system, a document management system and time and billing software, which is the foundation these agents need. The realistic first year gain is around 60 hours a week across the firm, close to 3 to 4 percent of your capacity, focused on the tasks your lawyers and paralegals like least. Nothing an agent produces should leave the firm without a named person approving it, and every draft should point back to the source document. Start with deadlines, contract first-pass review and billing preparation, because those are the easiest to measure and the least risky.

maturity.label: Early
maturity.note: You have the systems in place (Microsoft 365, practice management, document management, time and billing) but almost no AI in daily work. Deadline tracking, contract review and time entry checks are still manual, so there is a clear starting point with low risk.

opportunities.title: Contract first-pass review against your playbook
opportunities.description: An agent reads each incoming contract and compares the clauses against your firm's standard positions and fallback wording. It returns a short list of deviations with the clause text and a link to the source, and a lawyer still makes every call.
before: Open the contract and read it end to end
Search past matters for a similar agreement
Check each clause against your standard positions by hand
Write a note listing the deviations
Send it to the responsible lawyer for review
after: Agent collects the contract from the shared mailbox or document management system
Agent extracts the clauses and flags deviations from your playbook
Agent drafts a summary note with clause references and source links
Human: senior lawyer reviews the flagged list and decides what to push back on
Human: lawyer edits the note and sends the advice

opportunities.title: Deadline and tribunal calendar agent
opportunities.description: An agent watches incoming court and tribunal correspondence, pulls out each deadline and adds it to the matter calendar with reminders at 14, 7 and 2 days. Your paralegals keep the final check every morning.
before: Read court letters and emails as they arrive
Write deadlines into the matter calendar by hand
Set reminders manually for each one
Check the calendar each week to see what is coming
after: Agent reads inbound court mail and email
Agent adds each deadline to the matter calendar with a link to the source document
Agent sends reminders at 14, 7 and 2 days
Human: paralegal checks new entries each morning and corrects anything wrong

opportunities.title: Time entry review and draft invoices
opportunities.description: An agent reviews the week's time entries against matter budgets and billing rules, flags entries with missing detail or the wrong matter, and prepares draft invoices. Nothing is sent until your billing team approves it.
before: Export time entries to a spreadsheet
Read each line for a missing narrative or wrong matter
Email fee earners about gaps and wait for replies
Build each invoice by hand in the billing system
after: Agent exports time entries and checks them against matter rules and budgets
Agent emails fee earners a short list of entries that need more detail
Agent drafts the invoices in the billing system
Human: billing specialist reviews the drafts and sends them

opportunities.title: Document review and bundle preparation
opportunities.description: An agent reads a set of documents, groups them by type, date and issue, and builds a first pass index and bundle. It lists the citations it finds so a paralegal can check them against the source.
before: Open each document one by one
Tag by type and date by hand
Build an index in Excel
Check citations in a legal database
Assemble the bundle and export it
after: Agent reads the document set and groups it by type, date and issue
Agent builds a draft index with page references
Agent lists the citations that need checking
Human: senior paralegal checks the index, corrects it and finalises the bundle

opportunities.title: Client question triage and draft replies
opportunities.description: An agent reads the shared client inbox, sorts questions by topic, client and urgency, and drafts replies to routine questions using your firm's standard answers. A lawyer reviews and sends every reply.
before: Check the shared inbox several times a day
Forward each email to the right lawyer
Lawyer reads the thread history
Lawyer writes the reply from scratch
after: Agent sorts the inbox by topic, client and urgency
Agent drafts replies to routine questions using your standard answers
Agent routes anything unusual to the right lawyer with a short summary
Human: lawyer reviews the draft, edits it and sends it

opportunities.title: New client intake and conflict check pack
opportunities.description: An agent takes inbound intake forms and emails, pulls out the key facts, creates the client record, and prepares a conflict check summary and a draft engagement letter for a person to approve.
before: Reception forwards the enquiry to a secretary
Secretary retypes the client details into the practice system
Secretary emails the client for anything missing
Someone runs a name search for conflicts
Secretary drafts the engagement letter from a template
after: Agent reads the intake form and replies to the client for anything missing
Agent creates the client record in the practice system
Agent runs the conflict name check and drafts a short summary
Human: secretary confirms conflicts and sends the engagement letter

opportunities.title: Data room and signature coordination
opportunities.description: An agent keeps the deal data room up to date, chases outstanding documents on a fixed schedule, and runs the e-signature sequence for closing documents. It sends a status note once a day.
before: Paralegal uploads and names files by hand
Email each party for missing documents
Track signature status in a spreadsheet
Send reminders one at a time
after: Agent files and names incoming documents automatically
Agent chases missing items on a set schedule
Agent runs the e-signature sequence and tracks status
Human: paralegal checks the daily status note and steps in where needed

opportunities.title: Client appointment scheduling and reminders
opportunities.description: An agent handles meeting requests by email, proposes times based on the lawyer's calendar, books the room or Teams link, and sends confirmation and a reminder the day before. Anything unusual goes to a secretary.
before: Client emails or calls for an appointment
Secretary checks several calendars
Secretary emails back and forth to agree a time
Secretary books the room and sends a confirmation
Reminder sent by hand the day before
after: Agent reads the request and proposes times from calendar availability
Agent books the room or Teams link and confirms by email
Agent sends a reminder the day before with the agenda
Human: secretary handles reschedules and anything unusual

opportunities.title: Weekly matter and performance reporting
opportunities.description: An agent pulls matter status, deadlines and billing figures into a one page weekly report with the exceptions highlighted. It flags matters that are off budget or behind schedule.
before: Partner asks each team lead for a status update
Operations manager copies figures from the billing system
Spreadsheet updated by hand
Report written and circulated
after: Agent pulls matter, deadline and billing data on a set schedule
Agent drafts the weekly report with exceptions highlighted
Human: operations manager checks the figures and sends the report

roadmap.title: Get the basics connected
items: Connect Microsoft 365, your practice management system and your document management system to the agent platform
Write down one firm rule: nothing leaves the firm without a named person approving it
Set up the deadline and tribunal calendar agent for the Employment Law team
Set up appointment scheduling and reminders for reception
Name one owner per team who checks agent output and reports problems

roadmap.title: Move into the legal work
items: Roll out contract first-pass review to Commercial Law, starting with supplier contracts
Roll out client question triage and draft replies to the Employment Law shared inbox
Roll out time entry review and draft invoices to Finance and Billing
Pilot document review and bundle preparation with two paralegals on one live case
Review hours saved and error rates at the end of week 12 before deciding on phase 3

roadmap.title: Cover the rest of the firm
items: Add new client intake and conflict check packs
Add data room and signature coordination for Commercial Law transactions
Add weekly matter and performance reporting for the managing partner
Extend document review and bundle preparation to all paralegals
Review the full year of results with your compliance advisor and set targets for year two

risks.risk: Client and matter data going into tools that are not approved for it
risks.mitigation: Keep every agent inside your Microsoft 365 tenant and your existing systems, sign a data processing agreement with each supplier, leave client names out of prompts where they are not needed, and apply the same confidentiality rules you use today.

risks.risk: A wrong draft from an agent being treated as final and sent to a client or a court
risks.mitigation: No agent output leaves the firm without a named lawyer or paralegal approving it, and every draft shows the source document and clause it came from. Reviewers check the source, not just the summary.

risks.risk: Lawyers who bill by the hour do not use the tools
risks.mitigation: Start with the tasks nobody wants to do (deadlines, time entries, bundling), show the time saved on the first two live matters, and track use per team each month so you can see who has adopted it and who has not.

risks.risk: Cost and setup time running past what you planned
risks.mitigation: Fix the scope of each phase, give each phase one owner, and stop and review before spending on the next phase. Do not start more than two new agents at once.

risks.risk: GDPR and Belgian bar rules not being met for personal data in the tools
risks.mitigation: Keep a short data processing register, set retention limits on anything the agents store, and check the setup with your compliance advisor before phase 2 begins.

kpis: Hours saved per week across the firm (target: around 60 by the end of phase 3)
Deadlines missed or entered late (target: zero)
Average working days from client question to reply
Share of draft invoices sent within 5 working days of month end
Average contract review turnaround in days
Share of agent drafts changed or rejected by a human reviewer (quality check)
